figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: Attention mass, recall, and error on Wan2.1-T2V-14B at 89.16% sparsity. (a) Sorted cumulative attention mass of 4-token key blocks; the band spans the 10th–90th percentiles of query blocks. (b) Top-$k$ recall: the fraction of each query block’s dense attention mass covered by the selected key blocks. Finer blocks keep more mass, and IBCS halves the gap of mean-pool to the oracle at $b{=}4$. (c) Relative $\ell_{2}$ error of the attention output against dense attention. Sampling with SIP on IBCS scores lowers the error 41% below oracle top-$k$ at $b{=}4$.
figures.headline: Finer key/value blocks retain more attention mass, and SIP sampling on IBCS scores lowers error below oracle top-k.
citing_sentences: As Figure 2(b) shows, shrinking the key/value blocks from 128 to 4 tokens raises the attention mass retained by oracle top-$k$ from 59% to 69%.
As Figure 2(b) shows, IBCS thereby halves the recall gap of mean pooling to the oracle top-$k$.
Attention mass, however, has a long tail: as Figure 2(a) shows, even the oracle top-$k$ keeps only about 69% of it with 10.8% of the keys.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: Overview of AB-Attention. (a) IBCS clusters each query block $Q_{i}$ into centroids $\bar{Q}_{i}$ with weights $w_{i}$, and scores every key/value block by the weighted attention of the centroids to its pooled keys. (b) SIP samples each block with probability $\pi_{ij}$ proportional to its score $S_{ij}$, so no block is excluded, and weights it by $1/\pi_{ij}$ to estimate full attention. (c) The kernel gathers the sampled blocks into full tensor-core tiles and attends to them with logits shifted by $-\log\pi_{ij}$.
figures.headline: Overview shows IBCS scoring, SIP sampling with inverse-probability weights, and kernel packing of sampled blocks into tensor-core tiles.
citing_sentences: As illustrated in Figure 3, AB-Attention selects key/value blocks much smaller than an execution tile and estimates the dense attention of each query block from a weighted sample of them.

abstract: Video diffusion transformers generate high-quality videos, but the quadratic cost of 3D full attention dominates their inference. Dynamic block-sparse attention reduces this cost by computing exact attention only on key/value blocks selected from current activations. However, its fidelity degrades under aggressive sparsity: blocks are scored from coarse summaries or formed by costly global clustering, pruned blocks vanish from the softmax, and whole tiles are kept or dropped even when only a few of their keys matter. To address these limitations, we propose Accurate Block Attention (AB-Attention), a training-free method that accurately approximates dense attention at high sparsity. Its Intra-Block Clustering Selector (IBCS) estimates block importance faithfully yet cheaply by clustering queries only within each query block, without permuting tokens. Sampling with Inclusion-Probability Weighting (SIP) then samples blocks in proportion to these estimates and reweights them by inverse inclusion probability, so that one pass estimates dense attention rather than truncating it. Finally, its kernel gathers key/value blocks much smaller than a tile into full tensor-core tiles, refining selection at no extra tensor-core cost. On Wan2.1 and HunyuanVideo, AB-Attention skips 89–92% of attention, whereas the baselines compute 1.8–3.6$\times$ as much, yet it still improves PSNR by up to 4.4 dB over the strongest baseline and achieves up to 2.23$\times$ end-to-end speedup. Our code is available at https://github.com/InfRec-Cardinal/AB-Attention.

sections.body: The section lists three limits of current dynamic methods: coarse or costly block importance estimates, top-k selection that discards blocks from the softmax, and whole-tile selection units. It proposes AB-Attention with three parts: IBCS for scoring, SIP for sampling with inverse-inclusion weights, and fine-grained selection with tiled execution. On Wan2.1 and HunyuanVideo, it reports skipping 89–92% of attention, baselines computing 1.8–3.6$\times$ as much, PSNR gains of 1.6–4.4 dB over the strongest baselines, and 1.84–2.23$\times$ end-to-end speedups on a single H20 GPU.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Dynamic block-sparse attention loses fidelity at high sparsity, and AB-Attention is proposed as a training-free fix.

sections.body: The section defines dense attention with its $\mathcal{O}(n^{2}d)$ cost and notes that FlashAttention reduces memory traffic but still computes all query–key interactions. It then defines sparse attention as adding a mask to the attention logits. Block-sparse attention keeps or skips query–key block pairs as a whole, and the section states that larger blocks improve hardware utilization but select more coarsely, while smaller blocks give finer selection but may reduce execution efficiency.
sections.heading: Preliminaries
sections.headline: Dense attention and block-sparse attention are defined as the baseline for the proposed method.

sections.body: IBCS clusters the queries of each query block into $R$ centroids using one $k$-means iteration, and scores each key/value block by the cluster-weighted softmax attention to its pooled keys. SIP samples $s$ blocks with inclusion probabilities $\pi_{ij}=\min(1,\lambda_{i}S_{ij})$ and weights each sampled block by $1/\pi_{ij}$, so one sparse pass estimates the numerator and normalizer. A fused kernel gathers the small sampled blocks into full tensor-core tiles without reordering tokens. Sampling plans are rebuilt every $C$ denoising steps, while attention is recomputed at every step.
sections.heading: Methodology
sections.headline: AB-Attention scores blocks with intra-block query clusters, then samples and reweights them to estimate dense attention.

sections.body: On Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, Wan2.1-T2V-14B and HunyuanVideo-T2V-13B, the method reports the best PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS against dense attention, with sparsity of 89.16% or 92.35% and speedups of 1.84–2.23$\times$. Its speedup on HunyuanVideo drops latency from 4399.03 s to 1974.61 s. In the ablation on Wan2.1-T2V-14B, removing SIP weights lowers PSNR by 4.00 dB and tile-level selection by 1.02 dB. The section does not claim gains on every VBench dimension; it states that VBench stays close to dense attention.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: AB-Attention gives the highest fidelity and speedup on three models, and its ablations show each component matters.

sections.body: The section groups sparse attention into static patterns such as Sliding Tile Attention and Radial Attention, and dynamic methods such as XAttention, SpargeAttention, SVG2 and DFSAttn. It describes correction-based methods, including Rectified SpaAttn, PISA and SVG-EAR, which compute selected blocks exactly and approximate the rest. It also surveys other acceleration routes such as fewer denoising steps, caching and quantization. It states that AB-Attention estimates both the numerator and the normalizer from one weighted sample of all blocks.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Prior sparse attention methods are grouped into static, dynamic, and correction-based designs, with AB-Attention positioned against them.

sections.body: The conclusion restates the method: IBCS scores blocks, SIP samples and reweights them, and the kernel packs small blocks into full tensor-core tiles. It reports 89–92% skipped attention and 1.84–2.23$\times$ speedups. The limitations state that the kernel is built for H20 GPUs and supports only forward inference, and that the evaluation covers three text-to-video diffusion transformers. Future work is named as kernel support for more hardware, broader models, and a trainable version with backward support.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: AB-Attention is a training-free sparse attention method, limited to H20 GPUs, forward inference, and three models.

sections.body: Appendix A covers farthest-first initialization of query centers, pooling of key blocks into two keys, systematic sampling without replacement, and unbiasedness of the Horvitz–Thompson estimates. Appendix B lists the Wan2.1 configuration: query blocks of 128 tokens, key/value blocks of 4 tokens, eight clusters per query block, and sample sizes of 2048 and 2272 blocks, along with the baseline hyperparameters. Appendix C gives the quality metric and latency protocol. Appendix D gives Table 3, the PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS sweep over selection block sizes from 4 to 128.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix gives the sampling and estimator derivations, model configurations, baseline settings, latency protocol, and the block-size sweep table.
